attempts.summary: Discovered the physical topology (node1 eth3↔node3, node2 eth3↔node4 private links; node1 eth1↔node2 eth1 and node1 eth2↔node2 eth2 as the two independent uplinks). Kernel bonding/LACP was unusable because virtio NICs on this platform don't report link status to the bonding driver (mii_status stuck DOWN despite carrier being up), so I implemented redundancy at L3 instead: two /31 point-to-point links between node1/node2 with ECMP static routes (fib_multipath_hash_policy=1) carrying traffic for the node3⇄node4 private subnets across both uplinks, with automatic route withdrawal (kernel 'dead linkdown' nexthop marking) on link failure. Verified both baseline connectivity, ECMP flow-spreading across both links, and full node3↔node4 reachability surviving either link (eth1 or eth2) being taken down individually, with restoration confirmed after each. Persisted the configuration (systemd self-healing oneshot service on node1/node2; NetworkManager static profiles on node3/node4) after discovering and fixing a boot-race where a later SONiC container-startup event transiently reset interface state. Completed the mandatory node-restart protocol on all four nodes sequentially (preserving quorum/redundancy throughout), each showing a changed boot_id and full recovery of the redundant-uplink data path and node3↔node4 connectivity.
